_comment: Canonical role-registration expectations. Source of truth for role surface coverage (b80f0bdf). Every role here is part of the DELIVERY vocabulary's role subset; per-role keys override roleDefaults. A surface marked true must exist and verify; false = deliberately absent (do not create). governance = receipt-issuing allowlist (harness-srv KNOWN_EXECUTORS), only for roles that emit receipts. kind = address class per Ruling 13 (de5d538f): every entry under roles is kind=role — the only kind carrying a delivery obligation. INVARIANT (Ruling 24, 8a466f98) - the roles<->delivery relation is a UNION, NOT equality: roles.json (union) address-kinds.json is a SUBSET OF tackle.roles, and tackle.roles is permitted to be a STRICT SUPERSET. The two tables do different jobs: tackle.roles is the DELIVERY vocabulary, while this pair is the REGISTRY. A registered non-role address may legitimately hold a delivery row - that row records the address, not a delivery obligation - and `delivery: never` constrains the inbox pointer, not row existence. So neither side implies the other: a key here need NOT appear in tackle.roles, and a tackle.roles name need NOT appear here. Equality would compel the withdrawn `DELETE FROM tackle.roles WHERE name='big-pickle'` (tester e5538da4, upheld-as-retracted and moot in Ruling 24 section 4). Non-role addresses (alias/telemetry) live in config/roles/address-kinds.json and must NOT be added here. Every entry states kind explicitly (Ruling 25) - all 28 do, so an absent kind is not a supported state, not a default. Add a new role here + emit its artifacts, then run bin/verify-roles.py.
